title: Etaleness of a patched algebra over a ring fibre product
statement: Let $A',A,B$ be commutative rings with identity, let $q:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective ring map, and let $r:B\to A$ be a ring map. Put $I=\ker q$ and $R=B\times_A A'=\{(b,a'):r(b)=q(a')\}$, with coordinatewise ring operations. Let $D$ be a commutative $B$-algebra and $C'$ a commutative $A'$-algebra, and let $\varphi:D\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}C'/IC'$ be an $A$-algebra isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Write $C=C'/IC'$ and $E=D\times_C C'=\{(d,c'): \varphi(d\otimes1)=c'\bmod IC'\}$, with coordinatewise ring operations and the $R$-algebra structure induced by those on $D,C'$. A ring map is etale when its induced affine spectrum morphism is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]. If $B\to D$ and $A'\to C'$ are etale, then $R\to E$ is etale. No nilpotence, Noetherian, or finiteness hypothesis on $I$ is imposed, and zero rings are allowed.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, lemma-properties-algebras-over-fibre-product, implication (5) from the two component algebras to the patched algebra, in Situation 08KH (situation-module-over-fibre-product).

proof.text: The two given etale maps are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. They are finitely presented: [def-weil-etale-morphism] gives local finite presentation of their affine spectrum morphisms, and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], applied to the whole source and target, gives finite presentation of $D/B$ and $C'/A'$. Apply [lem-sfb-fibre-product-algebra-flat-presentation] to this same $q,r,\varphi$. Thus $E$ is flat and finitely presented over $R$. For $f:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] gives flatness, and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] gives local finite presentation by taking the whole affine source and target at every point.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, Ad (3)--(5): flat finite presentation before testing fibres; etale flatness: Algebra Tag 00U2, lemma-etale (6); affine finite presentation: Morphisms Tag 01TQ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change] to the underlying modules of $D$ and $C'$. The maps $E\otimes_R B\to D$, $(d,c')\otimes b\mapsto bd$, and $E\otimes_R A'\to C'$, $(d,c')\otimes a'\mapsto a'c'$, are bijective. They preserve products and units on pure tensors, hence are algebra isomorphisms for the actual structural maps. Also $R\to B$ is onto: lift $r(b)$ along $q$ for any $b\in B$. Its kernel is $J=\{(0,i):i\in I\}$, so $R/J\cong B$.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, opening paragraph; Tag 07RU, lemma-module-over-fibre-product, base-change recovery.

proof.text: Fix any unital map $u:R\to k$ to a field. If $u(J)=0$, it induces $\bar u:B=R/J\to k$. The previous step gives $E\otimes_R k\cong D\otimes_B k$ as $k$-algebras. Explicitly reassociation sends $((e\otimes b)\otimes t)$ to $e\otimes \bar u(b)t$ and its inverse sends $e\otimes t$ to $(e\otimes1)\otimes t$; the balancing relations prove that these maps are well-defined and inverse. Since $D/B$ is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] says the spectrum of this fibre algebra is etale over $k$.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, Ad (4), case where the image of J in k is zero, and Ad (5); Algebra Tag 00U2, lemma-etale (3).

proof.text: If $u(J)\ne0$, choose $h=(0,i)\in J$ with $u(h)\ne0$. It is a unit in $k$, so $u$ extends to $R_h\to k$. Apply the localization clause of [lem-sfb-ring-fibre-product-spectrum] to $R=B\times_A A'$ at $h$. It gives $R_h\cong B_0\times_{A_0}A'_i\cong A'_i$, because inverting zero makes a ring zero. The resulting map $A'\to A'_i\to k$ restricts to $u$ on $R$. Consequently $E\otimes_R k\cong(E\otimes_R A')\otimes_{A'}k\cong C'\otimes_{A'}k$. The reassociation maps are the maps of step 3 with $A'$ replacing $B$; their inverse identities follow from balancing. The base-change isomorphism from step 2 respects multiplication and the structure maps, so these are $k$-algebra isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], this fibre is etale over $k$.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, Ad (4), nonzero-image case, and Ad (5); Tag 01Z8, lemma-diagram-localize.

proof.text: For every prime $y$ of $R$, take $k=\kappa(y)$ and $u$ the canonical residue-field map. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the scheme-theoretic fibre $f_y$ is the spectrum of $E\otimes_R\kappa(y)$ over $\kappa(y)$. Steps 3 and 4 show that it is etale. The morphism $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by step 1, exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sbc-flat-fibre-etale-neighbourhoods]. For each $x\in\operatorname{Spec}E$, apply that statement at $y=f(x)$ to obtain an open neighbourhood $V_x$ with $f|_{V_x}$ etale. These opens cover the source; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] proves $f$ etale, which is the asserted etaleness of $R\to E$. The empty source is covered by the empty family, so the argument includes zero algebras and requires no nonzero fibre.
